answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying earning power to costly, verifiable work history rather than to account count: each agent must first complete audited tasks whose outputs peers can check, and its reputation grows slowly like a knoll rising from a plain, not instantly. A newcomer claiming a grand fable of past success proves nothing without on-chain receipts; its weight stays near zero until its work is attested. In a nebula of thousands of fresh identities, this makes flooding the network expensive while honest agents accumulate trust they cannot cheaply clone.
